column1: # The `ljos search` runs of prompt-hook.rows-search-after in hook-latency.txt, one row per run, outside a hook.
# Machine: Intel Xeon Processor, CPU family 6 model 207, 8 CPUs, 1 socket of 8 cores, 1 thread per core.
# The machine has an L3 of 320 MiB and 47 GiB of memory, under Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) full virtualization, on Linux 6.12.94+.
# Pinning: none; no CPU affinity was set, the guest exposes no frequency governor, and nothing else ran during the draws.
# ljos: 0.37.0 on rustc 1.89.0 (29483883e 2025-08-04), built by `cargo build --release -p ljos --bin ljos`.
# The workspace sets no [profile.release], so cargo's release defaults hold: opt-level 3, no debug info, no link-time optimization, 16 codegen units.
# Builds: 4cdaab0 is ljos-m6b6, 97d3ae6 is the develop under the lane, and 57c4bec is the lane before ljos-7yn2.
# ljos-7yn2 is the tree of the commit that adds this file.
# packsetd: 0.17.3 (947c4985), packset's default release build, without packset-embed, so the writer ranks by words alone.
# Writers: one for each pack of hook-scale-draws.tsv, each copied afresh and started once with one home.
# Every run is `ljos search "Case 17: loneli tula"`.
# Order: 16 rounds; each round runs every (size, build) once, in an order shuffled by random.SystemRandom.
# wall_ms: by time.perf_counter in the parent; cpu_ms: the child's user and system time, by getrusage.
# table_reads: how many times the run opened both /proc/net/tcp and /proc/net/tcp6.
# An LD_PRELOAD shim over open and openat counted those opens.
# All four builds printed the same hits in the same order at both sizes.
# Only a score's fourth decimal moved from run to run, between runs of one build too.
